body-dense.purpose: Bullet columns beside a strip or sheet.

takeaway.purpose: The single sentence on a direction sign at the bottom of a content slide.

sign.purpose: Uppercase airfield-sign legends: bay labels, page numbers, station placards.

label.purpose: Uppercase column heads, sheet title bars, and station roles.

data-id.purpose: Strip callsigns in B612 Mono; never wraps.

data-label.purpose: B612 Mono caps for row keys and field captions; never for paths or anything with a period.

code.purpose: File names, paths, and commands in Overpass Mono.

hand.purpose: Grease-pencil handwriting only: initials and short notes, slightly rotated.

shadows.name: sign-cast
shadows.purpose: Mandatory and direction signs with their black rim; location signs and page numbers use the cast alone.

shadows.name: strip-in-holder
shadows.purpose: Plastic lip highlight, contact line, and cast under every flight strip.

shadows.name: paper-on-board
shadows.purpose: Paper sheets lying on the console.

shadows.name: chip
shadows.purpose: Small paper tags: file names and evidence tags.

shadows.name: takeaway
shadows.purpose: The heaviest sign on the slide.

shadows.name: console-key
shadows.purpose: Raised key cap; pressed, it travels 2px and the contact line shrinks to 1px.

shadows.name: recessed-well
shadows.purpose: Code blocks; the release-board panel deepens the cast to 18px 34px.

shadows.name: in-flight
shadows.purpose: A strip lifted off the board during a go-around.

motion.name: fs-ease
motion.purpose: House ease: fast out, long settle. Used for slot, print, cock, cross, and the strip transition.

motion.name: slot
motion.value: fs-slot 560–900ms fs-ease backwards; from translate 56px 0, opacity 0.35; 70–160ms stagger
motion.purpose: Strips and list items arrive sideways into their bay.

motion.name: print
motion.value: fs-print 800–900ms fs-ease backwards; clip-path inset(0 0 100% 0) and translateY(-28px) to rest
motion.purpose: A strip or sheet prints top-down.

motion.name: drop
motion.value: fs-drop 520ms fs-ease backwards; from translate 0 -46px, opacity 0.3; 140ms stagger
motion.purpose: A pile of freshly printed strips lands.

motion.name: ink
motion.value: fs-ink 380–700ms ease-out backwards; clip-path reveal left to right
motion.purpose: A grease mark is written after its object lands.

motion.name: cock
motion.value: fs-cock 520ms fs-ease backwards; to translateX(26px) rotate(-1.4deg)
motion.purpose: A strip is pushed out of line to flag it.

motion.name: clear
motion.value: fs-clear-green / fs-clear-red; --holder amber to green or red in the last 18–30%; 400ms ease on --holder changes
motion.purpose: The holder changes color only when state changes.

motion.name: cross
motion.purpose: The cleared cover strip crosses the hold line.

motion.name: go-around
motion.purpose: A strip lifts off the board and drops back into hold.

motion.name: handoff-token
motion.purpose: The review token travels worker, reviewer, worker, reviewer, you; its holder changes with each pass.

motion.name: active
motion.purpose: Amber pulse on the box being worked, only while a presenter-started board runs.

motion.name: incident
motion.purpose: A 4px red ring flashes on a strip that trips a health gate.

motion.name: transition-strip
motion.value: 650ms; incoming pushes in from 100%; outgoing slides -32%, fades, brightness 0.55
motion.purpose: Default Marp slide transition: the board pushes to the next bay.

motion.name: transition-handoff
motion.purpose: Clear-then-arrive so only the morphing hero strip is visible mid-flight.

motion.name: morphs
motion.value: view-transition-name: fs-hero (one per slide), fs-route (route band)
motion.purpose: Carry one strip bay to bay across consecutive slides; disabled under reduced motion and print.

motion.name: settle-ceiling
motion.purpose: Every slide's motion settles within 4.7 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2); gated by fs-live (audience view, visible tab, not printing, no reduced-motion preference).

narrative.overview:
The deck is a night tower cab seen from the controller's seat: a graphite strip console under one warm lamp, buff card-stock flight strips in amber, green, and red plastic holders, red grease-pencil marks, and airfield signs. Every AI-written change is a strip, and a strip moves to the next bay only when a person writes its clearance. Every visual device is an object that cab would contain, and the slides argue for release discipline by handling those objects, not by decorating a page.

Density is that of a working board on a fixed 1280×720 frame: one claim per slide, stated as the headline; one composed board, sheet, or strip stack under it; and at most one direction-sign takeaway pinned to the bottom. Material carries the hierarchy. The lit console is the room's voice, card stock holds evidence and documents, signs give instructions, and grease records human decisions. Type is sized for the back of a conference room.

The direction rejects two things by name: the neon AI-talk deck and the white corporate template. Motion is the mechanism, never ornament. Strips print, slot into bays, get cocked or ringed, collect grease ticks, change holder, and cross the hold line. Each slide's motion is finite, plays only on the live audience slide, and animates into a finished state that the markup already holds.
keyCharacteristics: Two lit materials: graphite console with lamp-colored text, and buff card stock with navy ink.
Saturated color only where it means something: airfield signs, holder states, grease marks, real lights.
Overpass for words and signs, B612 Mono for strip data, Overpass Mono for code and paths, Permanent Marker for grease only.
Physical depth from one overhead lamp: a hard contact line plus a soft cast, always straight down.
Finite motion that settles within 4.7 seconds into an authored static state, so print, PDF, and reduced motion lose nothing.

rules.name: The Real Objects Rule
rules.body: Saturated color always means something in the world: a sign's instruction, a holder's state, a person's mark, or a real light. It is never decoration. Edge Light marks links and focus, and the brand icons in the contact blocks keep their tuned colors. Light comes only from the overhead lamp, the faint edge light in the far corner, and real lights such as the stop bar on the cover.

rules.name: The Three Reds Rule
rules.body: Mandatory Red is a sign, Red Holder is a strip state, and Grease Pencil is a person's mark. Each red keeps its job, so never swap them.

rules.name: The Holder Is State Rule
rules.body: A holder's color changes only when the strip's state changes: amber means in progress, green means cleared, and red means held. A holder color is never picked for variety.

rules.name: The Back Row Rule
rules.body: At 1280×720, labels are about 18px or more and sentences about 22px or more. A few built sizes run under this floor (13–17px): printed captions in the base strip, empty-slot legends, the footer, and the release board's keys, column heads, and readouts. They are not steps on the scale, so never reuse them for new text.

rules.name: The Right Mono Rule
rules.body: B612 Mono prints strip data only: callsigns, field captions, and readouts. Its period renders left-shifted, so file names, paths, and anything else with a period go in Overpass Mono. Overpass's middle dot is also left-shifted, so `·` never appears in Overpass text. Separate items with the small Sign Yellow square used in the cover byline.

rules.name: The Hand Is Grease Rule
rules.body: Permanent Marker appears only as a person's handwriting: short, slightly tilted, and in Grease Pencil or Grease Under Lamp. The one exception is the release board's rubber-stamp LGTM, written in Faded Ink. The face is never used for headings or body text.

rules.name: The Lamp Overhead Rule
rules.body: All shadows fall straight down from the one lamp, with zero x-offset and black only. Objects lying on the board add a hard contact line under the soft cast. Lift is a longer cast, never a glow. Rings (a black sign rim, a yellow lit-position ring, a red incident ring) are outlines, not light.

rules.name: The Real Holder Rule
rules.body: A holder is a carrier the card sits in, built from layered backgrounds. Never fake one with a colored left border or a tinted card. The 2px tan rules between printed fields are print on the card and stay.

rules.name: The Fixed Infrastructure Rule
rules.body: Signs never move. They are the infrastructure the strips move past, so they get no entrance animation, no hover, and no lift.

rules.name: The Complete Without Motion Rule
rules.body: The authored markup is the finished state. Motion only animates into it, with backwards fills, so nothing lingers. Every effect is gated by the live audience slide (`fs-live`: visible tab, not printing, no reduced-motion preference) and settles within 4.7 seconds. Print restores the authored snapshot, and runtime-only content has a static twin.

dos: Do put every slide on Graphite Console (#1b2023) with Lamp Light text, and put evidence (strips, sheets, chips, quotes) on Buff Card Stock (#efe6cc) in Strip Ink (#1a2540).
Do end a content slide with at most one takeaway: a direction sign pinned bottom left, with clear air between it and the composition above.
Do show a change's state with its holder (amber in progress, green cleared, red held) and a person's decision with grease (tick, ring, strike, initials).
Do set callsigns, field captions, and readouts in B612 Mono, and file names, paths, and commands in Overpass Mono.
Do keep labels at about 18px or more and sentences at about 22px or more at 1280×720.
Do keep every motion finite. Play it only on the live audience slide, use backwards fills, and let it settle within 4.7 seconds.
Do author the finished state in markup, so reduced-motion, print and PDF, presenter, and no-JavaScript views show a complete slide, and give runtime-only content a static twin.
Do carry one strip across consecutive slides with the shared hero morph name, one hero per slide.
Do label illustrative boards, changes, and percentages as fictional or illustrative on the slide itself.
donts: Don't use the neon AI-talk look or a white corporate template. The lightest surface is buff card stock, and light comes only from the lamp, the faint edge light, and real signal lights.
Don't fake a holder with a colored left border or a tinted card. Build it from layered backgrounds, and keep the 2px printed field rules inside the card.
Don't swap the reds. Mandatory Red goes only on signs, Red Holder only on strips, and Grease only on a person's marks and the holds they cause.
Don't pick holder colors for variety or give the deck's strips a fourth state color.
Don't set file paths or anything with a period in B612 Mono, and don't put `·` in Overpass text.
Don't animate signs or loop motion. The only repeating motion is the active-box pulse while a presenter-started board runs.
Don't suggest lift with x-offset shadows, colored shadows, or glows. Lengthen the cast instead.
Don't reuse the sub-floor sizes (13–17px) of strip captions, slot legends, and release-board controls as a scale step for new text.
